items.context: The spec has scope set to scenarios/agent-manager but no acceptance_allow or acceptance_deny globs. Since this is a pure refactor (file splits within existing packages), all changes should be confined to the API directory. We need to define what paths are expected to change and what must not change.

options.label: Broad: scenarios/agent-manager/api/**
options.rationale: Allows any API file changes — simplest, covers main.go splits and all internal/ changes

options.label: Targeted: scenarios/agent-manager/api/main.go, scenarios/agent-manager/api/internal/handlers/**, scenarios/agent-manager/api/internal/orchestration/**, scenarios/agent-manager/api/internal/domain/**
options.rationale: Restricts to only the files identified in the plan — prevents accidental changes to adapters, database, etc.

items.notes: Option A recommended — while the plan targets specific packages, the wire.go and middleware.go extractions from main.go could touch the root api/ directory, and test files across packages may need minor adjustments.

items.context: The plan defines 4 phases (handlers split, orchestration split, domain split, main.go cleanup). These can be executed as a single atomic operation or as separate commits/PRs. The choice affects review granularity and rollback safety.

options.label: Single atomic commit for all 4 phases
options.rationale: Simplest review — one diff shows the full refactor. Avoids intermediate states. Best for mechanical moves.

options.label: One commit per phase (4 commits)
options.rationale: Easier to review each phase independently, can bisect if issues arise. Each commit compiles and passes tests.

items.notes: Option B recommended — per-phase commits make it easy to verify each step compiles and passes tests, and allow reverting a single phase if needed.

items.context: handlers.go contains ~15 shared utility functions (parseUUID, parseQueryInt, parseQueryIntStrict, parseInt64Strict, parseRunnerType, parseTaskStatus, parseRunStatus, writeJSON, writeProtoJSON, mapErrorCodeToStatus, toProtoErrorResponse, toJsonValue, etc.). These need a home after the split.

options.label: Keep all in handler.go alongside Handler struct
options.rationale: Minimal change — helpers stay where they are, just the handler methods move out. Simple and predictable.

options.label: Extract to handler_helpers.go
options.rationale: Keeps handler.go focused on struct/constructor/middleware. Cleaner separation but adds one more file.

items.notes: Option A recommended — the plan says 'pure mechanical split only', so keeping helpers in handler.go alongside the struct definition is the least disruptive. They can always be extracted later.

items.context: The plan mentions ~800 lines as a guideline. Some split files may still be large (e.g., handler_run.go could be 500-800 lines given the number of run-related endpoints). Need to confirm the threshold or if further splitting is needed.

options.label: Soft ~800 line guideline (plan default)
options.rationale: Reasonable upper bound. Allows some files to be larger if they're cohesive. Matches the plan.

options.label: Strict 500 line limit with further sub-splits
options.rationale: Forces smaller files but may create too many files and break domain cohesion.

options.label: No size limit — split by domain only
options.rationale: Focus purely on domain cohesion. If handler_run.go is 800 lines but all run-related, that's fine.

items.notes: Option A recommended — the plan already defines this as a guideline, not a hard limit. Domain cohesion matters more than arbitrary line counts.

items.context: The codebase has 105 stdlib log.Printf/Println calls mixed with 53 logrus structured logging calls. The exploration identified this as a critical inconsistency. However, the current plan is scoped as a 'pure mechanical split' with no behavior changes. Should logging standardization be added to scope?

options.label: Exclude — keep plan as pure file split
options.rationale: Stays true to the plan's no-behavior-change constraint. Logging cleanup is a separate backlog item.

options.label: Include as Phase 5 — standardize to logrus
options.rationale: Natural follow-on since we're already touching most files. But expands scope beyond mechanical moves.

items.notes: Option A recommended — logging standardization changes behavior and test expectations. Better as a separate backlog item to keep this refactor safe and reviewable.

items.context: Three runner adapters (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) share significant logic (~1400-1569 lines each). Extracting a common base would reduce ~2000 lines of duplication. However, this is structural refactoring, not just file splitting.

options.label: Exclude — out of scope for this item
options.rationale: Runner adapters are in the adapters/ layer, not in the targeted monolithic files. This is a different refactor.

options.label: Include as Phase 5 — extract common runner base
options.rationale: High-value deduplication. But changes interfaces and behavior, unlike the rest of the plan.

items.notes: Option A recommended — runner deduplication is structurally different from file splitting (it creates new abstractions). Should be its own backlog item with separate testing.

items.text: The existing plan.md is already comprehensive and well-structured. It covers all 13 mandatory plan sections, defines clear phase boundaries, and has a strict 'no behavior changes' constraint. The plan was likely authored with good knowledge of the codebase — file sizes, method counts, and target layouts all match current codebase state.

Several files in handlers/ are already split by domain: pricing.go, stats.go, tools.go, websocket.go. The refactor follows this existing pattern, extending it to the remaining monolithic files. This is a proven pattern in the codebase.

plan_updates: No plan.md changes this round — existing plan is comprehensive. Workshop decisions refine execution details: acceptance boundaries (d1), commit strategy (d2), helper placement (d3), size guideline (d4), and scope boundaries for logging (d5) and runner dedup (d6).
